findings.statement: SCARB1 is the top-ranked target-profile gene and a surface protein, but staining is high in a vital organ (adrenal gland) and the GTEx proteome flags adrenal enrichment (tissue-specificity score [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.08]), which is an on-target off-tumour safety concern. Only a small share of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%]; a score does not show a conjugate would work.

The cell attribution of SCARB1 does not hold between single-cell datasets: the dominant group is myeloid in the Li dataset but tumour (RCC) in the Zhang dataset, and the tumour-cell share is only [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336] in Li versus [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582] in Zhang, so the tumour-intrinsic claim is uncertain.

SCARB1 protein is higher in tumours in the confirmatory DIA cohort and replicates (log2 fold change [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334]), in the same direction as discovery.

CA9 (known-target control) has an ADC suitability of [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647], with no kidney staining but high stomach staining and proteome enrichment in stomach (tissue-specificity [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19]); CSPA did not observe it at the cell surface, so gastric toxicity must be considered.

CA9 expression is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib (log hazard ratio per SD [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], adjusted p [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.padj=0.332]); the difference between arms is not significant (adjusted p [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]). This is a lead, not evidence of predictive value.

CA9 is flagged as a PBRM1 subgroup target candidate (TCGA mutant minus wild-type RNA difference [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148]) and is lower in ccB than ccA ([gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-1.551]), so a CA9-directed agent would matter most in ccA/PBRM1-mutant tumours.

CD70 (known-target control) has the best ADC suitability of the candidates ([gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746]) and no vital-organ proteome enrichment (maximum tissue-specificity [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=0.34]), but Human Protein Atlas staining data are not available, so normal-tissue safety is unconfirmed. CD70 was not tested in the confirmatory proteome cohort, which is not a failure to replicate.

Immune cells make a large share of CD70 tumour transcripts ([gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]), so the tumour-intrinsic signal is mixed with T-cell expression, and CD70 is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (log hazard ratio [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; log_hr_atezolizumab_bevacizumab=-0.383]), a lead from one arm.

CD70 cell attribution is inconsistent: the dominant group is T/NK cells in the Li dataset (tumour-cell share [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.345]) but tumour cells in the Zhang dataset (share [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.964]).

ENPP3 (known-target control) has suitability [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578] but high staining in normal kidney ([gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3.0]) and duodenum, so on-target kidney toxicity is a concern for a conjugate; it shows no vital-organ proteome enrichment.

SLC16A3 protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551]), and its one measured phosphosite also replicates.

SLC16A3 is a twelve-transmembrane transporter with a large tumour-cell share expressing it even in the weakest quarter of donors ([gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=43.7%]), but adrenal staining is high ([gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_staining_level=3.0]) and its short extracellular sequence limits antibody access; CSPA did not observe it at the surface.

NNMT protein replicates strongly in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]); it is a metabolic enzyme, not a surface protein, so an ADC is not the route.

NNMT is attributed to tumour cells in both single-cell datasets, with tumour versus proximal tubule log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=9.132] in Li and [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=5.573] in Zhang (only a few paired donors).

NNMT is not associated with differential benefit between nivolumab and everolimus in the CheckMate trial (adjusted p [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]), and the small nivolumab trial shows only a direction, so there is no treatment-selection evidence.

HK2 protein does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort: log2 fold change [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256] with adjusted p [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074], despite a strong discovery increase, so its target-profile rank rests on RNA and one cohort.

PPP1R1A protein loss does not reach significance in the confirmatory cohort (adjusted p [gene=PPP1R1A; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.17], only [gene=PPP1R1A; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_pairs=18] pairs), although the direction matches; the single phosphosite replicates. Treat the biomarker as unconfirmed at protein level.

PSAT1 protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]), but its one significant discovery phosphosite does not (replicating phosphosites [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); phosphosites_replicating=0]).

PSAT1 is higher in BAP1-mutant tumours (TCGA RNA mutant minus wild-type [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711]) and in ccB versus ccA ([gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=2.364]), but it is not a subgroup target candidate because the protein difference is not significant; this is a prognostic-subtype marker lead.

VWF is not an immune-cell transcript (immune share [gene=VWF; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.016]) and correlates negatively with the immune score ([gene=VWF; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=-0.369]), consistent with an endothelial or vascular signal rather than a tumour-cell one.

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) is associated with longer benefit on everolimus in the CheckMate trial (log hazard ratio per SD [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.everolimus_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=-0.183]) but the nivolumab versus everolimus difference is not significant (adjusted p [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]); no trial evidence supports using it to choose therapy.

PCK1 protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819]) and so do both measured phosphosites (count [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); phosphosites_replicating=2]), making it a robust loss-type biomarker, not a target.

caveats: Treatment-response associations come from single arms of about ninety patients or a sixteen-patient trial; no gene differs between arms after correction, so all are leads, not predictors.
ADC suitability scores rank surface accessibility and staining only; they do not show that a conjugate or radioligand would work, and CD70 lacks Human Protein Atlas staining data.

CA9, CD70, FABP6 and DUSP9 were not tested in the confirmatory proteome cohort (too few matched pairs); this is not a failure to replicate. Other top-ten genes that replicated (ENPP3, CYP2J2, ANGPTL4, ALDH6A1, SLC6A19, SLPI) were not given their own finding. Replication in L1CAM rests on few pairs.

EPAS1, PCK1, PSAT1 and several biomarker genes are tumour-loss or pathway genes without surface access; SCARB1 and CD70 cell attribution differs between single-cell datasets, and Zhang has few paired donors.
